survey: A stone park chess table with two stone stools on grass. The table is a thick square slab with rounded edges and a checkerboard inlaid flush in its top. One central pedestal holds up the slab: a short collar under the slab, a tapered square shaft with recessed panels, and a wide stepped plinth that sits flat on the grass. The stools are turned stone drums with a round cushion-like seat, a narrow waist and a wide stepped base. Both stand flat on the grass, one on each side of the table, facing the camera at a slight three-quarter angle. Everything is grounded and casts a contact shadow. The slab's overhang is modest and centred over a solid pedestal, so it could stand. The stools are round and match each other in profile. No parts pass through each other, float or are added without reason.
